the design and performance characteristics of integrated-circuit operational amplifiers that exhibit low susceptibility to electromagnetic interference-induced failures.

the step-response time constant (T _{s} ), which is the time required for the output to rise from 10 to 90 percent of the final value of a step input, should be minimized in the design of integrated-circuit operational amplifiers to achieve the best EMI immunity.
, for the integrated-circuit opamp, a fast and stable step response is a prerequisite for low EMI-induced failure probability.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EMI-induced failures in integrated-circuit operational amplifiers can be minimized by designing for a fast step response.
the EMI susceptibility of an integrated-circuit operational amplifier can be predicted by measuring its step response.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of low-EMI opamps can be accomplished by using a simple design methodology based on the step response of the opamp.
the EMI-induced failure probability can be reduced by increasing the slew-rate of the opamp, and by increasing its gain-bandwidth product.
